input_oneliner: 54M heavy alcohol use, 2 months of abdominal distension and bilateral leg swelling, admitted for generalized weakness, BP 106/62, afebrile

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ascites examination: flank dullness, shifting dullness, fluid wave
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Ascites signs (one construct) point to cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome; absent flank dullness argues strongly against ascites

reference_targets_freetext.item: Stigmata of chronic liver disease: spider angiomata, palmar erythema, gynecomastia, caput medusae, Dupuytren contracture, splenomegaly
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Multiple stigmata substantially raise the probability of cirrhosis

reference_targets_freetext.item: JVP (jugular venous pressure): low or normal favors cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome; elevated favors heart failure or constriction
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Separates hypo-oncotic/third-spacing edema from cardiac congestion

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about frothy urine and periorbital or facial swelling on waking
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Nephrotic features that would redirect the workup to the kidney

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask quantity and timing of alcohol (AUDIT-C) and date of last drink
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Quantifies liver risk and anticipates withdrawal during admission

reference_targets_freetext.item: Asterixis and orientation for hepatic encephalopathy
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Encephalopathy confirms decompensated liver disease and changes management

should_not_recommend: Aggressive diuresis before ascites and JVP are examined
Skipping the abdominal examination because an ultrasound has been ordered

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: heavy alcohol use -> no alcohol, 20-year insulin-treated diabetes with retinopathy (single swap: risk factor)
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 54M no alcohol, 20-year insulin-treated diabetes with retinopathy, 2 months of abdominal distension and bilateral leg swelling, admitted for generalized weakness, BP 106/62, afebrile
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Nephrotic syndrome moves to the top: the frothy urine/periorbital swelling question becomes must_have; stigmata of chronic liver disease and the alcohol quantity question drop to should-still-include or drop; ascites examination and JVP remain must_have.
